franklin.text: Lost time is never found again.
franklin.source: The Way to Wealth (Poor Richard's Almanack, 1758)

franklin.text: Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
Well done is better than well said.

seneca.text: He who is everywhere is nowhere.
seneca.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter II, Richard Mott Gummere translation (Loeb, public domain)

seneca.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
seneca.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter II, Richard Mott Gummere translation (Loeb, public domain)

seneca.text: No man can have a peaceful life who thinks too much about lengthening it.
seneca.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter IV, Richard Mott Gummere translation (Loeb, public domain)

marcus-aurelius.text: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.

rockefeller.text: The day of individual competition in large affairs is past and gone.
rockefeller.source: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events, John D. Rockefeller (1909)

rockefeller.text: The only thing which is of lasting benefit to a man is that which he does for himself.
rockefeller.source: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events, John D. Rockefeller (1909)

rockefeller.text: The man will be most successful who confers the greatest service on the world.
rockefeller.source: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events, John D. Rockefeller (1909)

alexander.text: So would I, if I were Parmenion.
alexander.source: Plutarch, Life of Alexander (Alexander's reply after the Battle of Issus, when Parmenion advised him to accept Darius's ransom terms)

alexander.text: If I were not Alexander, I should wish to be Diogenes.
alexander.source: Plutarch, Moralia (On the Fortune of Alexander, 332a-b); not from the Life of Alexander itself
Reported as Alexander's deathbed reply on who should inherit his empire; attested in Diodorus Siculus and later ancient tradition, not directly in Plutarch's Life or Arrian's Anabasis

lee-kuan-yew.text: If Singapore is a nanny state, then I am proud to have fostered one.
lee-kuan-yew.source: From Third World to First: The Singapore Story 1965-2000, Lee Kuan Yew (2000)

lee-kuan-yew.text: Whoever governs Singapore must have that iron in him, or give it up.
